thread:
ariane: Nightly CI (candidate kernel sweep) flagged a regression on Ampere for mid-seq workloads (seqlen ~512). attaching raw CI link: https://ci.redwood/4156789123/logs :eyes:

sam: yikes, is it kernel selection or batching? quick glance shows a different kernel picked at runtime for seqlen=512 vs 256

josh: i saw that too. the pick heuristic bumped to the new 'packed-gemm-v2' variant for midseq on ampere, which increased latency ~12% on our microbench

maria: perf-bot summary pasted below — looks like KV-cache miss rate also increased around same run, might be correlated

perf-bot: nightly-sweep: candidate set=23 kernels; regression detected on model=groq-small, arch=ampere-a10g, seqlens=[384,512]; p90 latency +11.7%, cpu offload unchanged

sam: possible cause: new kernel assumes prefilled KV layout, but our runtime prefill heuristic changed earlier this week to aggressive prefetching -> cache thrash?

josh: can someone run the microbench locally with KV profiling turned on? command i used:
```bash
tools/bench/run_microbench --model groq-small --arch ampere-a10g --seq 512 --kernels candidates/packed-gemm-v2 --kv-stats --repeat 200
```

ariane: kicked that off on perf-lab-03, job id 9876. initial output: p90 142ms, before patch p90 126ms. attaching flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/fg/9876

maria: flamegraph looks like heavy time in `kv_cache::evict_if_full` and `packed_gemm::matmul_inner`

sam: hmm eviction shouldn't spike for midseq unless the prefill is evicting useful prefixes. what's our batch size distribution in that run?

opsbot: run-metrics: batch distribution: 1:18%, 2:47%, 4:22%, 8+:13% (median batch=2)

josh: median batch=2 is fine but kernel expects larger micro-tiles for throughput. if autotuner selected kernel based on throughput samples with batch=8+, it'll mispick for real traffic

ariane: proposal: adjust autotune gating to include median batch and kv-hit ratio as inputs before promoting a candidate; and add a safety rollback on nightly CI if KV eviction rate increases >5%

maria: agree. small patch to gating logic: require candidate to have >=95% KV-hit parity with baseline AND p90 <= baseline + 3% on median-batch workload

sam: i'll prototype a gating rule in the autotune harness today. quick test: run candidate selection offline with synthetic batch dist to validate picks

josh: also add an explicit fallback path: if runtime detects high eviction rate during warmup, switch to the previous kernel variant for first N tokens

ariane: filing a follow-up ticket and will signal-canary once gating change is in. ticket: ENG-RUN-4021

maria: cc @sam @josh — please drop short repro notes in the ticket with commands and perf links

opsbot: deploy-note: canary policy updated to include kv-hit check, pending PR #5123

sam: thanks. i'll run a nightly re-sweep after gating change merges and post results here. if anyone has additional microbench configs to try ping me

josh: leaving a short note — watch out for ampere variants with >256 kernels; our current pickscore math can overweight flop density vs cache friendliness

ariane: ok everyone, let's reconvene in ~2 days or sooner if CI shows regressions. :thumbsup:
